html:
The Basmachi movement was an armed revolt against Russian and then Soviet rule in Central Asia, from 1916 into the early 1930s, strongest in the Fergana valley and in the hills of eastern Bukhara, now Tajikistan.

It grew out of the revolt against wartime labour drafts in 1916 and the Bolsheviks' bloody destruction of the Kokand autonomy in 1918. Its bands, led by local chiefs and religious men, fought for land, faith and self-rule. The Ottoman general Enver Pasha tried to unite them and was killed fighting the Red Army in 1922 in what is now Tajikistan.

The Red Army wore the movement down, while the Soviets won over some of the people by easing their policies on land and religion. Its last fighters crossed into Afghanistan. The new Tajik republic grew out of the lands it had held.
sum: The Basmachi movement was an armed revolt against Russian and then Soviet rule in Central Asia, from 1916 into the early 1930s, strongest in the Fergana valley and in the hills of eastern Bukhara, now Tajikistan.
